evidence.label: Pipeline fee
evidence.value: 0.25% of each swap's input, charged by the router on every hop and paid to Pipeline's treasury.
evidence.source: Pipeline docs/INTEGRATOR-GUIDE.md; constant text kept by Aviary

evidence.label: Router protections on swaps
evidence.value: The router moves your input into the strategy's vault, refuses the swap if you would receive less than your minimum, and never takes more than the amount you signed. You do not sign the call to the strategy, so it can pay you but cannot take from your accounts.

evidence.label: Custom actions
evidence.value: Any strategy instruction other than a swap is signed directly on the strategy; the router's protections and fee do not apply to it.

evidence.label: Bypass
evidence.value: A strategy may allow trades that skip the router; those pay no Pipeline fee and leave no swap event.

evidence.label: Vetting
evidence.value: Pipeline does not vet strategies; anyone can register one.

evidence.label: Router control on devnet
evidence.value: The router is upgradeable. Its upgrade authority 2yJJsmhvs2SBsKVtiKCG4wBJNoTH67aRNMhSwkupvUHZ is also its admin, who can pause swaps, market creation and registration.
evidence.source: Router ProgramData 3dpKiLED... and Config BmdeX3kW... read 2026-11-09 at slot 520324283

summary.text: In Canary's probe on 2026-11-09, selling straight after a tiny buy returned 48.99% of the SOL paid, so a round trip here loses about half.
The program has its own buy and sell that skip Pipeline, and so far more trades went that way than through Pipeline.
The key FWbh...vrKq can replace the code at any time, and has received half of the trading fees split so far.

claims.text: Each market appears to mint its token on buys and remove it on sales: the market itself holds the mint authority.
Besides Pipeline's instructions, the program has its own buy and sell, which trade without Pipeline's fee or swap record.
On the sampled market, 16 trades went through Pipeline and 23 directly; across its markets, 50 went through Pipeline and 52 directly.
Each trade, routed or direct, puts 0.30% of its SOL side into the market's fee vault.
Pipeline's fee account for this market holds 99.54% of the token's supply, taken as Pipeline's fee on the market's one sale through Pipeline.
The key FWbh...vrKq can replace the program's code at any time; it has not done so since deploying it on 2026-11-08.
The same key is the factory authority, and each time fees were split or used for buybacks, half went to its account.
The sampled token has no freeze authority, and only the market itself can mint it.
On 2026-11-09, 0.00001 SOL bought 4.064593969 tokens and selling them back returned 48.99% of the SOL; past trades show a buy at 139 and a sale at 67 lamports per token.
Quoting a sale larger than the token's supply crashed the program instead of returning an error.
A call to its Pipeline swap that skipped the router was refused, and exact-out trades are not supported.
Through Pipeline, the router refuses a trade that would pay you less than the minimum you set.
The program's own buy and sell are signed directly on it, outside the router's protections.
Its author's metadata link returns an error, and no public source was found.

unknowns.text: With no public or verified source, the price curve, and why a sale pays about half of a buy, are unknown.
Which actions only the factory authority may call.
Whether a sale works later or at larger sizes: the full exit test has not run.
